title: The Loop
summary: As in the ordinary trolley case, you can divert a runaway trolley away from five people onto a side track. But the side track loops back and rejoins the main line, so the trolley would come round and hit the five from the other side, unless something stops it. On the loop is one very large man, heavy enough to stop it. Judith Jarvis Thomson used the loop to test the idea that diverting is allowed because the one's death is only a side effect: here, the plan works only because the trolley hits him. Thomson thought diverting was still permissible, which puts pressure on that explanation.
citations: Judith Jarvis Thomson, "The Trolley Problem," Yale Law Journal 94, no. 6 (1985): 1395–1415
Alison McIntyre, "Doctrine of Double Effect," Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/double-effect/
